name: Trello
tagline: Kanban boards a team can actually keep up to date
description: Atlassian's lightweight kanban tool with boards, lists, cards and automations for small teams, and a free tier generous enough to run a real client project.
priceNote: Free plan; Standard is $5 per user/month billed annually ($6 monthly), Premium is $10 per user/month ($12.50 monthly) and Enterprise is $17.50 per user/month with a 25-seat minimum. Pricing as of October 2026; plans change — check the official site.
bestFor: Small teams that want visible work in progress without a project management rollout
pros: Boards are learned in minutes, so a team can be working on them the same afternoon
The free tier supports ten boards and up to ten collaborators, enough for real projects
Butler automation handles the tedious moves, like advancing a card when a label changes
It sits inside the Atlassian ecosystem, so Jira and Confluence connect without extra cost
cons: Boards are flat, with no native timelines, dependencies or workload views for complex work
Per-user pricing on Standard and Premium adds up once a client team joins the board
Automation runs are capped on Standard and the limits are not obvious from the pricing page
Premium Power-Ups run third-party code, which is a small supply-chain risk to consider

features.name: Boards, lists and cards
features.detail: Drag-and-drop work items with checklists, due dates and attachments

features.name: Butler automation
features.detail: Rule-based moves, assignments and notifications when things change

features.name: Multiple views
features.detail: Switch a board from kanban to table, timeline or calendar on Premium

features.name: Power-Ups and integrations
features.detail: Extend cards with Slack, Google Drive and dozens of other apps

features.name: Blueprints and templates
features.detail: Start from a proven workflow for software, marketing or agencies

features.name: Admin controls
features.detail: SSO, workspace controls and attachment policies on the upper tiers

useCases: Run a five-person client project on a free board without paying for anything
Track a content pipeline from idea to published with a simple card pipeline
Give an agency a per-client board template and spot capacity problems at a glance
Coordinate a marketing launch with a checklist per channel and an automation per stage
bestForWho: Teams of up to about ten who need simple, visual task tracking without a project management rollout.
verdict: Trello is still the fastest way to get a team organised, and for small companies that is exactly what a project tool needs to be. The board model is obvious after two minutes, so there is no rollout project and nobody has to learn a methodology before the work starts. Butler quietly removes the card-chasing that eats admin time, and the free tier is genuinely usable for a client project with a handful of people. The limitation is depth: boards stay flat, so dependencies, timelines and capacity planning all require a different tool or a discipline of keeping the board tidy. Paid pricing also arrives per user, which makes the decision easy if only four people ever touch the board and awkward if a client joins it, but for visual, lightweight coordination it is hard to beat.
